description: Positional parameters ($1, $2, ...) over a VALUES source, used everywhere an expression can appear: as a bare select item, as a function argument, NESTED inside another call, in arithmetic between two calls, under CAST in both directions, in string concatenation, as a CASE subject across several rows, inside COALESCE where the first two positions are NULL, inside SUBSTRING, and mixed with plain positional items in one SELECT list. Converted 1:1 from query/PositionalParameterExpressionsTest (now retired); the Java deliberately compared numeric cells by VALUE rather than by boxed class, because the carrier legitimately differs between the embedded engine and a live account over JDBC - the testkit comparator normalises numbers the same way, so the claims survive unchanged.

steps.sql: SELECT ABS($1), UPPER($2), LENGTH($3) FROM VALUES(-5, 'hello', 'world')
SELECT ABS($1) + ABS($2) AS sum FROM VALUES(-3, -4)
SELECT CAST($1 AS VARCHAR), CAST($2 AS INTEGER) FROM VALUES(123, '456')
SELECT CASE WHEN $1 > 10 THEN 'High' ELSE 'Low' END FROM VALUES(5), (15)
